what: ORI-WEIGHT: the orientation arm's missing parameter, now implemented
the_diagnosis: Five of the nine orientation-limited clips are still unadopted (e09 e10 e13 e20 e21) with an oracle bound of +0.318 of AUC each -- about +0.053 on the entry mean, enough to pass wte09fl at 0.54183 and crisiumnih at 0.58226 on tier1-auc. The one arm tried there, second-wave B4x, raised the orientation shaping std from 0.3 to 0.8 and gained +0.0206 on e00: 6% of the bound.
why_it_underperformed: Two things have to be right and B4x fixed only one. At std 0.3 rad a clip sitting 49.8 deg out earns exp(-(0.87/0.3)^2) = 0.0002 of the term, so there is no gradient at all; std 0.8 raises that to 0.31 and fixes the gradient. But the term's WEIGHT was hardcoded at 1.0 against body_joint_position's 5.0, so the policy had a gradient and a fifth of a reason to follow it. Raising the std without the weight is half the change.
what_was_implemented: brev/patch_object_orientation.py now takes --weight as well as --std, and it reaches BOTH the dataclass default and the YAML -- the YAML carries the value the runtime reads, so parameterising only the default would have made the flag a silent no-op. Two tests added: that the weight reaches both files, and that a non-positive weight is refused. Full suite 513 passed, ruff clean.
a_formatting_bug_the_tests_caught: My first version formatted the weight with {:g}, which renders 1.0 as '1' and changed the patched text. The patch's entire safety model is exact string matching against upstream, and a test pins that text, so it failed immediately. Fixed with !r, which keeps 1.0 and 5.0 in the house style.
the_arm_it_makes_runnable: orientation std 0.8 with weight 5.0 on e09 e10 e13 e20 e21, five clips at 0.5 h each = $1.70. Pre-register the bar as the standing Tier 1 rule: AUC improves and no board regresses. Even a fifth of the oracle bound is +0.064 per clip, about +0.011 on the entry mean, which passes wte09fl for a rank point.
status: Implemented, tested, NOT run -- the remaining credit is committed to the transfer queue, and the transfer is demonstrated where this is not.
